site.title: HotGap app
site.tagline: Will more pay leave you with less?
landing.check.title: Check my benefits
landing.check.body: Answer five short questions. See what happens to your help if your pay goes up.
landing.places.title: Compare places
landing.places.body: See which states have the worst gaps. Tap a state to see how big its cliff is.
landing.privacy: We do not save what you type. No sign up. No tracking.
flow.zip.confirm: Looks like you live in {state}. Is that right?
flow.zip.bad: That ZIP code does not look right. Please check it.
flow.zip.territory: We are sorry. We can not help in this area yet.
flow.family.spouseDisabled: Does your spouse have a disability?
flow.family.kids: How many kids live with you?
flow.housing.q: What do you pay to live there each month?
flow.housing.hint: Rent or house payment. Your best guess is fine.
flow.childcare.q: What do you pay for child care each month?
flow.childcare.hint: If family watches your kids for free, put 0.
flow.gets.q: Which of these do you get now?
flow.gets.hint: Most families do not get these. Say yes only if you do.
flow.gets.housing: A housing voucher or housing help
flow.pay.q: What do you make now, before taxes?
flow.pay.hours: How many hours a week do you work?
flow.pay.spouse: What does your spouse make, before taxes?
loading.title: Doing the math…
loading.body: We check your help at 100 pay levels. This can take a few seconds.
result.verdict.always_up: Good news. When you earn more, you keep more.
result.verdict.always_up.body: We did not find a spot where more pay leaves you with less.
result.verdict.cliff_ahead: Near {wage}, more pay can mean less money.
result.verdict.cliff_ahead.body: If your pay goes past {wage}, you could lose about {drop} a year. People call this a benefits cliff.
result.verdict.in_danger_zone: You are in a tough spot right now.
result.verdict.in_danger_zone.body: At your pay, you may end up with less than someone who earns a bit less. Once pay gets past {escape}, earning more helps again.
result.verdict.in_danger_zone.body_stuck: At your pay, you may end up with less than someone who earns a bit less. In the pay range we checked, we did not find a spot where you come out ahead again.
result.verdict.cliff_behind.body: The big drop is below your pay now. From here, more pay means more for you.
result.chart.title: Your pay vs. what you keep after health costs
result.chart.yLabel: Money left after health costs, per year
result.chart.dangerZone: Rough zone: more pay, less money
result.chart.alt: A chart of what your family keeps after health costs, as your pay goes up. Shaded parts show where more pay means less money.
chart.drop.hint: Tap a red dot to see what you lose.
chart.drop.marker.label: A drop near {pay}. You'd lose about {amount} a year here. Tap to see what ends.
chart.drop.card.amount: At {pay}, more pay drops what you keep by about {amount}.
chart.drop.card.none: A few kinds of help would get smaller here.
result.why.title: Why does this happen?
result.why.currentValue: Right now this is worth about {amount} a year to you.
escape.title: How help changes as pay rises
escape.healthCost: You'd pay about {amount} a year for health coverage at this pay.
escape.safe: Past {wage}, more pay always helps you.
escape.safeNever: Even at the top of our chart, we did not find a fully safe spot.
escape.leap: To clear the worst rough zone in one move, it takes a raise of about {amount} a year.
escape.leapMore: To clear the worst rough zone in one move, it takes a raise of at least {amount} a year.
escape.reach: Clearing the cliffs here takes about {income} a year. At that pay, you'd out-earn about {pct}% of families like yours in {state}.
escape.reachNever: Even families like yours with the top pay here still hit rough spots.
result.county.note: Numbers use your county where we can.
result.honesty.title: Please know
result.honesty.body: This is a guess based on public rules. Your caseworker decides your real benefits. Rules change. Do not make a big choice on this number alone.
result.honesty.model: Numbers come from PolicyEngine, an open rules model. We may not know every local program.
result.honesty.health: In many states, losing Medicaid means moving to other coverage you help pay for. In some states there is no low-cost plan.
result.honesty.reach: The reach numbers use pay from work for families like yours (Census ACS PUMS). They show how common that pay is. They are not your odds of getting there.
toggles.title: What if you get more help?
toggles.hint: Turn these on or off to see how your cliffs move.
result.fallback.banner: We could not get your exact numbers right now. These are numbers for a family like yours in your state.
error.title: We could not get your answer.
error.body: The math service did not reply. Your answers were not saved. Please try again in a minute.
program.wic: food help for moms and babies (WIC)
places.title: Compare places
places.intro: Pick a family. See where they could lose the most money by earning more.
places.pick.title: Pick a family to compare
places.pick.state: Or pick a state from a list
places.metric.title: Compare states by
places.metric.leap: The pay gap to clear it
places.legend.title: How much can they lose?
places.legend.leapUpTo: Needs a jump of up to {amount}
places.legend.noneFound: We did not find a cliff for a family like this in any state.
places.map.alt: A map of the United States. Darker states mean a bigger possible loss for this family.
places.map.altLeap: A map of the United States. Darker states mean a bigger jump needed to get past the worst rough zone for this family.
places.map.stateLabel: {state}: can lose up to {loss} a year.
places.map.stateLabelLeap: {state}: needs a jump of up to {amount} to clear it.
places.panel.headline: In {state}, a family like this can lose up to {loss} a year by earning more.
places.panel.headlineLeap: In {state}, a family like this needs a jump of about {amount} a year to clear it.
places.panel.safe: Earning more is fully safe here after about {amount} a year.
places.panel.safeNever: Even at the top of our chart, this family still hits rough spots here.
places.panel.leap: Getting past the worst rough zone takes a raise of about {amount} in one move.
places.panel.leapMore: Getting past the worst rough zone takes a raise of at least {amount} in one move.
places.panel.reach: The income to get fully clear here is more than about {pct}% of families like this earn.
places.panel.reachNever: Even families like this with the top pay here still hit rough spots.
places.panel.honesty: These are numbers for the family you picked, not your family. Check your own numbers on the home page.
places.panel.healthNote: These numbers also count what a family pays for health coverage, not just cash help.
places.panel.reachNote: The reach numbers use pay from work for families like this (Census ACS PUMS). They show how common that pay is. They are not this family's odds of getting there.
places.panel.assumptions: We assume the grown-ups are 30. Pay is their only income. We also assume no rent or child care cost.
places.panel.baseline: We also assume they do not get waitlisted help like Head Start or a housing voucher. Most families do not.
places.error: We could not load this state. Please try again.
